results.summary_before: This is a hardware implementation of the BCH (15, 7) error-correcting code, which can correct up to two bit flips in a 7-bit message using an 8-bit checksum. It has two modes selected by the encode_enable pin: encoding produces the checksum from a clean message, and decoding recovers the original message from a corrupted message plus checksum. The datapath is pipelined into syndrome calculation, error location and Chien search stages, giving a three-cycle latency and one message per cycle throughput at 50 MHz. No external hardware is required, though LEDs may be used to visualize inputs and outputs.

results.summary_before: This project implements a Constant False Alarm Rate (CFAR) signal detection engine that processes a 14-bit ADC input and displays detection results on a 7-segment display. It uses an IIR running average to estimate the noise threshold and compares the input signal against a scaled threshold to detect targets. The design requires an external 14-bit signal source and a 7-segment display for visual feedback. It is a simplified version without a buzzer, optimized for area-constrained silicon.

results.summary_before: The DDS Sine Chirp Beacon is a direct digital synthesis sine source with fixed-tone, chirp, and dual-tone modes, providing an 8-bit parallel sample and a 1-bit PDM output. It uses a 24-bit phase accumulator and a 64-entry sine lookup table, with chirp modes that sweep the frequency over time. The design can be used to excite resonant systems or scan audio paths. External hardware such as an R-2R DAC, RC low-pass filter, and piezo buzzer or amplifier is required to use the outputs, and the documentation is clear about its operation.

results.summary_before: This project implements five analog comparators using only digital standard cells from SKY130. The comparators take analog inputs and produce digital outputs, with some requiring an external clock. Testing requires a signal generator and oscilloscope to observe the comparator behavior. It demonstrates analog functionality using digital cell libraries.

results.summary_before: Tiny PI Controller implements a simple PI controller with a UART interface for configuration and data exchange. It is designed for control systems applications like motor control, where the derivative term is not needed. The controller can receive sensor values and output computed PI values over UART, with configurable Kp, Ki, and setpoint. It requires an external 12 MHz clock and a UART-capable device.

results.summary_before: This is a minimal design that implements a single AND gate with two inputs and one output. The documentation provides a complete truth table showing that the output is high only when both inputs are high. No external hardware is required. The project is a beginner-level Wokwi exercise with very little additional detail.
